settings.title: Heavy Industries

settings.support: Documented procedures, trained collectors, specimen-integrity and chain-of-custody controls, maintained equipment, consistent records and scheduled program reviews.

settings.title: Transport & Logistics
settings.challenge: Dispersed and shift-based operations must account for different sector rules, fitness-for-work expectations and practical site conditions.
settings.support: A role- and site-aligned process, trained collectors and supervisors, equipment controls, chain-of-custody documentation and central records.

settings.title: Government & Critical Services
settings.challenge: Public accountability, workforce diversity and high-consequence roles require a consistent process that also respects privacy and dignity.
settings.support: Defined responsibilities, consistent collection and escalation procedures, competency records, secure reporting and a clear audit trail.

settings.category: Hospitals · Aged Care · Disability · Community Services
settings.title: Healthcare & Community
settings.challenge: Duty of care must be balanced with informed consent, confidentiality, privacy and dignity across varied care settings.
settings.support: A setting-appropriate method, trained staff, clear consent and privacy steps, specimen-integrity controls and secure, restricted records.

settings.title: Workplace & Corporate
settings.challenge: Different job risks and limited in-house specialist knowledge can lead to inconsistent policy decisions, testing steps and records.
settings.support: A risk-based policy, supervisor guidance, fit-for-purpose equipment, a documented process and periodic review as the workplace changes.

settings.heading: What's included in a Managed Compliance Program?
settings.text: The scope is tailored to your organisation. It can include a review of your policy and procedures, nationally recognised collector training through HLTPAT010, appropriate testing technology and consumables, implementation support, documentation and ongoing program reviews.

settings.heading: How is this different from just doing HLTPAT010 training?
settings.text: HLTPAT010 builds an individual's specimen-collection skills. A managed program connects that capability with your policy, testing methods, equipment, documentation, escalation steps, records and program governance.

settings.heading: Do you provide the testing devices?
settings.text: Yes. Andatech can recommend and supply fit-for-purpose alcohol and drug testing devices, consumables, servicing and calibration options, with connected reporting where appropriate. The final mix depends on your policy, testing method, sites and operating conditions.

settings.heading: Can this cover multiple sites?
settings.text: Yes. Multi-site consistency is a core use case. The program can define common roles, procedures, equipment controls and records while accounting for the practical needs of individual sites, shifts and jurisdictions.

settings.heading: How does the compliance review work?
settings.text: We begin by understanding your policy, roles, sites, testing methods, equipment, training, collection and chain-of-custody steps, records and escalation process. You then receive a prioritised view of capability gaps and practical next steps. It is a program review, not a legal audit or legal advice.

settings.heading: What's the ROI calculator based on?
settings.text: It uses only the figures you enter: annual test volume, outsourced test and call-out costs, the share you expect to bring in-house, one-off setup costs and ongoing annual costs. It compares potentially avoided outsourced costs with the program costs and shows the formula, so the result is transparent and indicative rather than a quoted saving.

settings.heading: Can I combine this with HLTPAT010 training?
settings.text: Yes. HLTPAT010 training can form part of the capability plan for team members who need to collect specimens. Training requirements, delivery and eligibility should be confirmed for your organisation and participants before enrolment.
